content: 1. Norethindrone acetate may reduce the effects of insulin degludec and insulin aspart due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins can impair glucose tolerance, so diabetic patients should be monitored for glycemic control. 2. Ethinyl estradiol can decrease the effects of insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, and insulin lispro through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Diabetic patients should be monitored closely for glycemic control. 3. Norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol may reduce the effects of inhaled insulin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, requiring close monitoring of diabetic patients. 4. Ethinyl estradiol can increase the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Conversely, isavuconazonium sulfate can increase the levels of ethinyl estradiol, necessitating avoidance or alternative drugs. 5. Istradefylline increases the levels of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. At a dose of 40 mg/day, it increased peak levels of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 6. Itraconazole increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may elevate plasma hormone levels, requiring close monitoring. 7. Ivosidenib decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effects. 8. Ketoconazole increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may elevate plasma hormone levels, necessitating close monitoring. 9. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. This interaction requires close monitoring. 10. Lansoprazole decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and requires caution and monitoring. 11. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of lapatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Larotrectinib may increase the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 13. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Lenacapavir increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase the risk of adverse reactions, requiring close monitoring. 15. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 16. Lesinurad decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives should not be relied upon alone, and additional nonhormonal methods are recommended. 17. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Letrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 18. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of levodopa, levofloxacin, and other medications by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral administration of iron salts should be separated by at least 2 hours from these drugs. 19. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of mexiletine and midazolam by inhibiting hepatic metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Monitor closely for increased effects. 20. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ferrous fumarate, norethindrone acetate, and ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Conversely, it may increase the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 21. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms and requires monitoring. 22. Minocycline and other antibiotics may decrease the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, posing a low risk of contraceptive failure. 23. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during coadministration. 24. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol by plasma protein binding competition. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 25. Moxifloxacin and other antibiotics may decrease the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, posing a low risk of contraceptive failure. 26. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider alternative or additional contraceptive methods. 27. Nafcillin decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of contraceptive failure. 28. Ethinyl estradiol increases the effects of naratriptan and other drugs by unspecified mechanisms, potentially increasing adverse effects. 29. Nefazodone increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Nelfinavir increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal methods are recommended. 31. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by increasing CYP enzyme activity. Dosage modifications may be needed. 32. Neomycin decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, posing a low risk of contraceptive failure. 33. Nevirapine decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 34. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of nicardipine and nilotinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by increasing metabolism. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 36. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, posing a low risk of contraceptive failure. 37. Nizatidine decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms and requires monitoring. 38. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the effects of nortriptyline by decreasing oxidative metabolism, potentially increasing antidepressant serum concentrations and adverse effects. 39. Ofloxacin decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, posing a low risk of contraceptive failure. 40. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and alternative methods are recommended. 41. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir are contraindicated with ethinyl estradiol due to the risk of significant ALT elevations. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating these drugs. 42. Omeprazole decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms and requires monitoring. 43. Otesecozole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicity of ethinyl estradiol. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 44. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 45. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of oxytetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 46. Pancrelipase decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor closely for reduced iron levels. 47. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms and requires monitoring. 48. Paromomycin decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, posing a low risk of contraceptive failure. 49. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of penicillamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms and requires monitoring. 50. Penicillin G aqueous decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by increasing metabolism, increasing the risk of contraceptive failure.
